problem: Strong piti in two sits, then only gentle piti; is it blocked?
teacher: Intensity varies; it only matters that it is definitely pleasant. Ask whether you can enjoy it more, not whether you can make it stronger.

problem: Pushing with too much effort; headaches.
teacher: Overshooting effort. Treat effort as a dimmer.
Undershooting effort; try a bit more.

problem: A strong bodily movement as energy opened; 'this was scary'.
teacher: A normal energetic effect; nothing to worry about; it fades as samadhi deepens.

problem: Guilt and sadness about feeling joy while others suffer pulled attention from piti.
teacher: A habit from conditioning; meet it with compassionate inquiry; if not helping after some minutes, do something else.

problem: The pleasant sensation rises a little and stops; tempted to help it along.
teacher: Do nothing. Do not try to make it grow. It grows unevenly and then takes off.

problem: Breath became very shallow or seemed to stop; took a deep breath.
teacher: Shallow breath is a sign of access concentration. Do not take a deep breath; it weakens concentration.
Too comfortable produces sloth and torpor.

problem: A lot of frustration from trying to grasp jhana; could reach some piti but not jhana.
teacher: Relax the effort and reduce the craving; treat it like falling asleep; if frustrated, stop for the day.
Loosen it, or try an uncomplicated pleasant memory.

problem: Early attempts: grasping pushed the pleasure away.
First jhana is too much pleasure; agitating.
teacher: (Own diagnosis) normalises with practice. Brasington: second jhana is much more soothing; shift from the physical pleasure to the joy.

problem: An inner critic saying he was doing it wrong, would never get there, did not deserve pleasure.
teacher: (Own diagnosis) access came from getting over self-hatred, not concentration training.
One of the most common mistakes.

problem: Anxiety when the breath sensation vanished.
teacher: (Own account) a threshold obstacle met again in later practice.

problem: Did not trust the experience at first; overthinking.
teacher: (Own advice) relax, have fun, do not overthink it.

problem: Sadness, anxiety and dread after a couple of days of meditating.
teacher: (Repliers) go gently; get support; not a failure.

problem: Ringing in the ears became irritating.
teacher: The aversion, not the sound, is the problem; do not get into an aversive relationship with it.
uncovered: The coach has no category for aversion to a specific distraction.
